analyst_view.overall: Sporting (10th, 9 points) host Manchester United (17th, 6 points); a win would put Sporting close to the top eight, while United need points to stay in the play-off spots. Both have new coaches: Paulo Fonseca at Sporting, and Mauricio Pochettino at United, whose first game ended in a 4-0 defeat at Liverpool on Sunday after Leny Yoro was sent off early (a domestic ban, not a Champions League one). United are without Matheus Cunha, banned for this game after his red card against Roma (UEFA confirmed a one-match ban), and the numbers do not list him; Sesko, Baleba and Ugarte (counted) are also out. Sporting have their internationals back after a 4-0 cup win, but Ioannidis, Debast and Flávio Gonçalves are doubtful and Nuno Santos is out. No referee is named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals and already take Sesko off United (-4.5%). Cunha led United's attack at Anfield and is banned here, which the numbers don't know, so I take about 5% off, to about 2.8. United's leaky defence (19 conceded in 6) is already in the numbers, and Sporting's doubtful striker Ioannidis keeps me from going further either way.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.7 corners, with United slightly more of them and Sporting trimmed 4% for their recent count. Fonseca's Sporting build through the middle and Pochettino has had only days to change anything, so I stay at 8.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards, already lowered 11% for Sporting's quiet recent record and raised about 6% for United's busy one (16 cards in 6). Cunha's ban removes one hot-headed player, but that is small, and no referee is named yet, so I stay at 3.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.9 shots, with United's recent shot volume adding about 10% to their side. Without Cunha, one of their busiest shooters, and with Sesko out, United's attack rests on Mbeumo and Fernandes, so I trim a little, to about 27.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.2 shots on target, split evenly. Cunha's ban, which the numbers don't see, takes away one of United's main finishers, and Sporting may be without Ioannidis, so I trim slightly, to about 9.9.
